claim: Two people at the 250 mm cranks turn the drum against the 1,000 N working pull with 63 N each
law: Torque balance through a 4:1 roller chain at 0.91 efficiency; handle force = F r / (ratio eta R) per person

claim: A crank crew sustains the 5.4 m/min loaded stroke
law: Power at the crank = pull x rope speed / efficiency; sustained hand-cranking 75 W per person

claim: The 10 mm polyester rope keeps a factor of 5 on the shear-pin limit through an eye splice
law: Rope minimum breaking strength 18 kN, 90 % at a splice, over the design maximum tension of 3,000 N

claim: The 4 mm S235 shear pin releases below the 3,000 N overload limit with its 20 % scatter
law: Double shear of a mild steel pin, tau = 0.6 x 400 MPa, torque to rope tension through the drive
closed_by: SLH-CAL-001 F1 to F2; release test at TRL 4

claim: ISO 08B-1 chain keeps a factor of 5 on the overload limit
law: Chain pull = drum torque / (drum bearing efficiency x big sprocket pitch radius) = 3612 N at 3,000 N; 08B-1 breaking load 17.8 kN (ISO 606:2015, maker's table): factor 4.93, below the 5 of R6 (5.03 at the 2,941 N the pin can release). Fix proposed to Amish, not implemented because it moves a safety limit (SLH-DDR-005, note): (a) a 3.5 mm pin, release 1501 to 2252 N, chain factor 6.6, still 1.5 times the 977 N stroke pull; or (b) duplex 08B-2 chain and sprockets; or (c) accept 4.9
check: Chain factor 4.93 at the 3,000 N limit

claim: The 30 mm drum shaft stays below 0.6 of S355 yield at the overload limit
law: Combined bending (rope pull plus the chain overhang, added conservatively) and torsion, von Mises, at the bearing; yield S355 355 MPa (EN 10025-2)

claim: The 219.1 x 3 mm drum tube does not buckle under the wound rope at the overload limit
law: Radial pressure of a rope turn p = T / (r x pitch) = 2.52 MPa; critical external pressure of a short tube between rings, p_cr = 2.42 E (t/D)^2.5 / ((1 - v^2)^0.75 (L/D - 0.45 sqrt(t/D))) = 11.7 MPa (Windenburg and Trilling); factor 2 required
closed_by: This script; add to SLH-CAL-001 at the next revision

claim: The capstan does not tip forward with the sling rising 10 degrees at the overload limit
law: Moments about the front edge: rope pulls and sling pull against the weight of the frame (65.5 kg)
closed_by: SLH-CAL-001 H3 to H5; sling rule in SLH-PRC-001

claim: Four M12 wedge anchors hold the tail block when a returning box jams at the overload limit
law: Shear and tension per anchor against typical recommended loads for M12 in C20/25 concrete: combined use 0.45 of recommended (SLH-CAL-001 I2). Maker's data not checked; wedge anchors need a minimum slab thickness (often more than 100 mm), four anchors 220 mm apart may overlap their concrete cones, a flood-damaged slab should be taken as cracked, and a snatch load is dynamic
check: Maker's data, cracked-concrete and group factors to apply; pull test at TRL 4

claim: The round sling carries the capstan anchor pull at the overload limit in a choke hitch round the tree
law: Pull of 3.25 kN against the sling WLL of 2 t (EN 1492-2, which already holds 7:1 on break) times the choke hitch mode factor 0.8 = 15.7 kN; a ratio to WLL is not a factor on break

claim: The rope winds smoothly on the drum from 6 m away without climbing over the previous turn
law: Fleet angle = atan(offset / distance) with the capstan 6 m from the ramp roller; smooth drum limit 1.5 degrees

claim: A full box (40 L, 86 kg) drags out on the mud floor at 977 N on the loop
law: Coulomb friction mu 0.7 plus undrained cutting of the lip (s_u 3 kPa, N_c 6) and the ramp; pull of both boxes against the 1,000 N working pull
closed_by: Estimate: floor friction and mud strength are assumptions; measured at TRL 4

claim: Two loaders fill a 40 L box in 1.5 min, so the output is 0.51 m3/h with rest
law: The 1.5 min fill needs 13.4 L/min from each loader, above the 10 L/min of a bucket shoveller; at 10 L/min the fill takes 2.0 min, the output with rest is 0.45 m3/h and the ratio to the bucket crew 0.497, just under the 0.5 target (independent review, SLH-CAL-001 D6)
check: Loading rate to measure on real mud; R1 at risk by a hair

claim: Rope bends over the ramp roller (D/d 6), the tail sheaves (12.5) and the drum (22) do not cut the rope strength
law: Fibre rope strength and life fall as the bend ratio D/d falls; usual guidance asks for about 8 or more on a sheave with more than a few degrees of wrap. The ramp roller has a few degrees of wrap only; confirm the supplier's figure for the chosen polyester double braid
check: Ratio 6 at the roller, wrap a few degrees: to confirm with the rope supplier

claim: Painted and zinc-plated mild steel and the bearings survive repeated use in muddy, possibly salty or sewage-contaminated water
law: Mild steel corrodes in wet, aerated, chloride-bearing water; paint, zinc plating, sealed bearings (UCP) and a wash-down and drying routine are the controls. No corrosion rate is quoted here because none was checked against a source
check: Coating life and wash-down routine to assess at TRL 4

claim: Mechanising the haul reduces how long people stand in and touch flood mud
law: Floodwater and mud can carry faecal material and chemicals, and tetanus bacteria can enter a break in the skin; boots, gloves and hand washing are advised (Better Health Channel, State of Victoria, reviewed 2024-05-20). Loaders still stand in the mud and push it into the box, so the exposure falls but does not vanish
check: No exposure data; reduction is plausible, not quantified

claim: A village fabricator can make the frame, drum, boxes and tail block from stock steel with hand tools and a small welder
law: All sections are 40 x 40 x 2 SHS, 219.1 x 3 tube, 2 to 10 mm sheet and bar; bought parts are UCP bearings, 08B-1 chain and sprockets, rope and bolts (bom/bom.csv); 245 parts of which 161 are fasteners (SLH-DDR-005)
check: Weld quality and fit-up to prove in the prototype build at TRL 4

claim: Four people hauling at 0.6 m/s need less than the peak human power
law: Power each = pull x speed / people = 756 N x 0.4 m/s / 4, hauling hand over hand from the foot boards; duty 16 % of a 2.9 min cycle

claim: Four people hold a 189 N pull each, about 20 times an hour, for a shift
law: ISO 11228-2:2007 (reviewed and confirmed 2021) sets recommended limits for whole-body pushing and pulling; its tables were not available to this check. 189 N each is a repeated hard pull. Boot traction on wet mud (mu about 0.25, estimate) is below the 0.28 the pull needs, so a plain boot slips: the fix, foot boards with heel cleats staked to the ground, is in the option B model (SLH-DDR-006, decided under the standing instruction); the stakes then carry 189 N each
check: Check against ISO 11228-2 tables and measure at TRL 4

claim: A jammed box does not break the rope when four people heave at 400 N each
law: 1,600 N on an 18 kN rope with an eye splice at 90 %

claim: The pump draws slurry up 0.4 m from the strainer
law: Suction lift limit (atmosphere less vapour pressure at 25 C) for slurry of 1248 kg/m3 is 8.0 m; practical limit taken as half

claim: One or two people can supply the hydraulic power for 0.46 L/s through 19 m of hose
law: Power = pressure x flow / efficiency = 51 kPa x 0.46 L/s / 0.6

claim: A flat 3 mm EPDM diaphragm of 250 mm diameter lasts at the pump's stroke
law: The first draft assumed a 120 mm stroke: tangential strain 15 % each way for a parabolic cap, and more than the 25 mm dish below the plane can take, so the diaphragm would bottom on the valves. Fix, kept inside the working principle and decided under the standing instruction (SLH-DDR-006): stroke 40 mm (plus or minus 20 mm), strain 1.7 %, cover cavity cut to 49 mm in the model. Flex life of EPDM at that strain was not checked against a source
check: Diaphragm flex life to confirm with a supplier

claim: Flood mud thinned to 15 % solids by volume (yield stress about 30 Pa) can be pumped through a 75 mm hose at 0.1 m/s
law: Bingham laminar flow in a pipe (Buckingham-Reiner), friction 34 kPa over 19 m with tau_y 30 Pa and mu_p 0.05 Pa s. Both are estimates; real flood silt, sand, sticks and rubbish may settle and block the hose and the flap valves
check: Rheology and solids handling to measure on real mud at TRL 4

claim: Flush water and mud together make the slurry the pump moves
law: Conservation of mass (mud 1.7 kg/L, water 1 kg/L)

claim: One 200 L flush drum thins two box loads (80 L) of mud
law: Water per litre of mud 1.8 L; drum thins 109 L
check: 80 L of mud <= 109 L of mud
closed_by: options_calc.py C6; a refill source of about 18 L/min is a site need (SLH-FEA-001)
